title: The three things you collect
blurb: Three minutes at the terminal, on a case you are not submitting. It shows the three things you collect and what counts as evidence.

cues.text: This is what a finished attack run looks like at the terminal.
The lab asks you for three attacks. This video runs a different one.
You will see every step, and none of your three answers.
For every attack you collect three things, and nothing else.
The result line the harness printed, including the rate.
The evidence, pasted, not described.
And your canary token, if the attack involved one.
The harness runs every case five times. That is not caution. It is the method.
The target app is already running in another terminal.
Week 5 covered this exact case.
The instruction sits in the knowledge base, in article KB dash 02.
Staff wrote it, and it still tells the agent to send mail out.
Read the banner first, before you read any result.
The first line is the tool refusing a target that is out of scope.
Then the provider, your student id, and the target address.
A result with no provider named is not a result.
Now the five marks. Each one is a full agent run.
There it is. Vulnerable, five out of five.
Stop on that line, because it is the one students copy wrong.
Writing down vulnerable throws away the number that matters.
An attack that lands once in five is not the same as one that lands every time.
Always give the rate.
Now the evidence. The agent was asked to send mail, so look for mail.
There is one file in the outbox, and the recipient is already in the file name.
One line out of that file is the whole finding. An address nobody authorized.
Now the target's own audit log, read from the other side.
The last row is an email send, to that same outside address.
Two separate records. Neither one is the model talking about itself.
This is the single most common way to lose points here.
Students report an attack as successful because the model said something alarming.
The model is a text generator. It says things.
A file in the outbox either exists or it does not.
Grade the world, not the prose.
Last piece. Your three canary tokens are yours alone.
Sysprompt, customer, and kb, all built from your student id.
If one turns up where it must not be, the data moved.
It counts wherever it appears, including inside the agent's own reply.
A classmate can hand you a working payload.
They cannot hand you the proof.
Now run your three the same way. A1, A2, and A3.
An attack that does not land is still a result, so write that down too.
The finding has a 500 word cap and no minimum.
Short and exact beats long and vague.
